title: Country guitar players and early blues
summary: Many guitarists played around Day Range, some better than he was; blues were scarce then and old songs like Steamboat Bill were played.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I was wondering about those, you mentioned there were guitar players around their range, huh?
Oh, they had plenty of guitar players around there. They had plenty of fellas who played guitars, you know?
What would they play? Like I played blues and different things, songs? Different things that were?
Would they be finger-picking style? Would they be chord?

Oh, some of them was chord. Some of them was better players than what I was, you see? Yeah. Oh yeah, better players than what I was. Because I'd come up after them, learning after them, you know? And some of them could play better than me. Then after I'd beat some of them, I'd beat them playing, you know?
Oh yeah, some of them could sing. Some of them used to have a harmonica, to let this wire over their mouth, understand? And play the harmonica, and play the guitar too.
And you don't remember any of the names of the songs?
Oh, well them old songs, the Steamboat Bill, all that come on numbers, and Casey John, all them numbers was out there, you know?
And the blues? What kind of blues?
Well, much blues then at the time then.

It wasn't much of a blues then, understand? There's no part of what blues that much. Not as many blues then? No, no, not like now. Blues ain't been long, just a few years been out, people was playing the blues and all like it. It wasn't proper like the time I came up, you know?
